changes.change: post() and ack() commit each part's attempt with the bridge's outbox authority (delivery_store) before any of its bytes, record each part's outcome (confirmed, refused, rejected, or ended without or with finality after an absolute wait and a bounded drain), and on a failure hand off the unconfirmed remainder or queue the whole call; with no committed answer they publish one immutable fallback file per call instead, and raise Queued only once it is durable. Login and channel creation have absolute deadlines. A silent run's post is refused and never queued in any form. outbox_append(), outbox_claim(), outbox_summary(), reserve() and queued_entry() are removed: this release writes no outbox.jsonl row.

changes.change: The bridge runs the outbox authority (delivery_store.Authority: the only opener of outbox.db, on its own thread, serving outbox.sock; a start that failed part-way is finished at the next pass) and its flush: it imports fallback files and the legacy outbox without outbox.lock, ends gone writers' attempts, abandons (E8) or, for its own announcements, adopts (E9) their entries, reconciles from current state (R1, R2), dead-letters after 24 hours with a content-free alert row, gives every eligible entry its attempt, and retires claims and writes dead letters under a bounded outbox.lock. It indexes every verified message (V1) before its checkpoint moves; a failed index invalidates any catch-up of that channel, which completes nothing until a replay from the preserved checkpoint indexes it; keeps record coverage in the authority, writes the pending queue, ledger and dead letters durably, and announces with a derived entry id, saving held_announced only once the announcement is durable. The file-based claimed-outbox, reservation and attribution state is removed.

The outbox's one SQLite authority (#19): the store and its transitions, reconciliation, the bridge-only authority server and its request protocol, clients, fallback files and the lock-free import (design revision 8).
Shared fakes for the outbox tests: a chat server that commits before it answers, an injected clock, invented processes, an in-process authority and a filesystem model that drops unsynced changes.
#19's failing-first regressions: the whole-post repost, a failed confirmation record and a stopped outbox.lock holder, run against the code before and after the fix.
#19's acceptance 1-10 and design revision 8's posting scenarios against a fake server and an in-process authority.
The outbox authority's rules: attribution, finality, fragments, accounting on every part, collection, alerts, A12 and attested outcomes (#19).
The outbox's file boundaries: fallback files, the legacy claim and durable exports, with power losses and a stopped lock holder (#19).
The bridge-only authority and its request protocol over socketpairs: stopped clients, floods, replays, epochs, unavailability and the one opener (#19).
The bridge's outbox side: coverage and indexing, bounded setup, its announcements and E9, and the authority thread (#19).
A crash at every boundary of design revision 8's section 5.5, one case per row (#19).
